title: Sergeant Major of the Marine Corps (SgtMaj) PMOS, DC M&RA
raw_text:
5.     MOS 8991, Sergeant Major of the Marine Corps (SgtMaj) PMOS, DC M&RA

    a. Summary. Assists the CMC as Senior Enlisted Marine in the Marine
Corps. Advises the CMC in matters pertaining to enlisted personnel and
assists the CMC in the performance of his duties. Performs such specific
duties as member of the CMC's enlisted performance board, member of the
permanent Marine Corps uniform board, and member of the CMC's party on all
visits and inspection trips to Marine Corps installations when enlisted



                                         3-508                        Enclosure (1)
 3156                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



personnel are involved. When directed by the CMC, assists staff agencies in
matters pertaining to enlisted Marines. Represents the CMC at the Staff
Noncommissioned Officers symposium.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Possess exemplary qualities of leadership.

        (2) Possess to an exemplary degree initiative, sound judgment,
industry, and dignity of demeanor.

        (3) Possess sufficient training, schooling (formal or OJT) to act
independently as principal enlisted assistant in all administrative,
technical, and tactical matters in a unit.

       c.   Requirements.   None.

       d.   Duties

            (1) Communicates ideas effectively at all levels.

        (2) Possesses to the highest degree the faculty for working in
harmony with officers, other noncommissioned officers, and civilians.

        (3) Demonstrates a comprehensive understanding of Marine Corps
organizations, missions, and staff procedures.

        (4) Possesses a comprehensive understanding of staff procedures and
inter-organization relationships including inter-service organization and
relationships at the highest levels.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Human Resources, Training, and Labor Relations Specialists, All Other 13-
1079.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     Administrative Specialist, 0111.

The Command Senior Enlisted Leader Occupational Field is comprised of the following two specialties: 8991, Sergeant Major of the Marine Corps and 8999, Sergeant Major-First Sergeant. Both specialties serve as the command senior enlisted leader, responsible to the commander for all matters that influence the readiness, effectiveness, and performance of the command. They are the institutional advocates of the organization’s history, traditions, customs, and courtesies and enlisted career human resource development. The Command Senior Enlisted Leader assists with communicating and enforcing the commander’s intent and guidance.

5. MOS 8991, Sergeant Major of the Marine Corps (SgtMaj) PMOS, DC M&RA a. Summary. Assists the CMC as Senior Enlisted Marine in the Marine Corps. Advises the CMC in matters pertaining to enlisted personnel and assists the CMC in the performance of his duties. Performs such specific duties as member of the CMC's enlisted performance board, member of the permanent Marine Corps uniform board, and member of the CMC's party on all visits and inspection trips to Marine Corps installations when enlisted personnel are involved. When directed by the CMC, assists staff agencies in matters pertaining to enlisted Marines. Represents the CMC at the Staff Noncommissioned Officers symposium. b. Prerequisites (1) Possess exemplary qualities of leadership. (2) Possess to an exemplary degree initiative, sound judgment, industry, and dignity of demeanor. (3) Possess sufficient training, schooling (formal or OJT) to act independently as principal enlisted assistant in all administrative, technical, and tactical matters in a unit. c. Requirements. None. d. Duties (1) Communicates ideas effectively at all levels. (2) Possesses to the highest degree the faculty for working in harmony with officers, other noncommissioned officers, and civilians. (3) Demonstrates a comprehensive understanding of Marine Corps organizations, missions, and staff procedures. (4) Possesses a comprehensive understanding of staff procedures and inter-organization relationships including inter-service organization and relationships at the highest levels.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
